item.title: Tone River Wetlands: Reed Marshes on Japan's Second Longest River — Guide
item.description: The Tone River, Japan’s second-longest river, has played a vital historical role as a trade and transport artery for the Kanto region since the Edo period. Where it approaches the Pacific in Ibaraki, extensive reed marshes and wetlands line the lower river, supporting a range of birdlife and offering a quieter, more contemplative landscape than the region’s more visited attractions. The wetlands are especially atmospheric in late afternoon, when golden light catches the tall reeds along the waterway.

item.title: Mangoku-ura: A Ramsar Wetland for Migratory Birds — Guide
item.description: Mangoku-ura is a shallow coastal inlet near Ishinomaki designated as a Ramsar Wetland — twice daily the tide exposes vast tidal flats that host thousands of migratory shorebirds including dunlin, golden plover and rare spoonbill in spring and autumn. The surrounding pine forest and salt marsh ecosystem was heavily damaged in 2011 but has recovered remarkably, with bird populations now higher than pre-disaster counts. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Ishinomaki, Miyagi Hours Always open; low tide for best flats viewing Admission Free Time needed About 1.
